Nirsevimab special situations (ages 8–19 months with chronic lung disease of prematurity, severe immunocompromise, cystic fibrosis criteria; American Indian/Alaska Native children 8–19 months; extra dose after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass) not encoded: ages are in months, timing is relative to the second RSV season, and eligibility relies on clinical detail (medical support in prior 6 months, weight-for-length percentile, imaging) not reliably in structured data.
RSV seasonal timing notes (October–March administration, jurisdiction-specific seasonality) and palivizumab interchange notes not encoded.

Maternal RSV vaccine (Abrysvo) at 32w0d–36w6d gestation, September–January, not encoded: depends on gestational age, season, and an either/or choice with infant nirsevimab; 'All other pregnant women: RSV vaccine not recommended' and 'Subsequent pregnancies: additional doses not recommended' are not-recommended statements, listed here only. Infants of mothers vaccinated in a previous pregnancy should receive nirsevimab — not encoded (requires maternal history linkage).

Rotavirus series not encoded: required dose count depends on product (Rotarix 2 doses vs RotaTeq 3 doses; default to 3 if any dose RotaTeq or unknown), ages are in months/weeks (minimum age 6 weeks, do not start on/after 15 weeks 0 days, max age 8 months 0 days for final dose), and the vocabulary lacks product-specific concepts.
Tdap during each pregnancy (preferably gestational weeks 27–36) not encoded: requires per-pregnancy window tied to gestational age.

Tdap rule does not credit DTaP inadvertently given at age 10–18 (which counts as the adolescent booster), and does not model that Tdap given at age 7–9 does not satisfy the booster while age-10 Tdap does; doses given at age 10 before MY-2 will not be credited. No dose-date-vs-birthdate logic is available.
Tdap/Td catch-up for ages 7–18 not fully vaccinated with DTaP (fully vaccinated = 5 valid DTaP doses or 4 if dose 4 at age ≥4 years) and Table 2 catch-up guidance not encoded.
Catch-up Tdap for ages 13–18 who have not received Tdap not encoded as a separate rule (13-year-olds are covered by the adolescent booster rule).
Wound management Tdap/Td (10-year vs 5-year intervals by wound type, Tdap preference for age ≥11, Tdap for pregnant adolescents) not encoded: depends on wound events and clinical judgment.
Rule IDs use concept tdap_vaccine; no new concepts introduced.
